text:
Maya R: Heads up — saw a weird perf pattern in the load-3 run: throughput dropped ~18% when we hit a steady stream of prefix cache hits.
Kevin L: Can you paste the profiler flame?
Maya R: Pasted snippet from the live trace: `serve:batch_form -> packer:select_windows -> kernel_selector` then long idle in queuing before send.
Sanjay P: Interesting. Are hits creating many short requests and the packer is holding waiting for tail-fill?
Maya R: Exactly. Most requests are KV-hit prefix + 4 tokens generate. Batcher tries to reach token_budget target and delays microbatches, increasing latency.
Lisa T: Was there a kernel fallback at the same time? We had the pax-kernel patch roll yesterday.
Maya R: We saw occasional kernel fallback jitter but the bigger impact seems to be packing policy: prefix hits look like short sequences so they get deprioritized and starve long-prefix prefill jobs.
Kevin L: Can you share the config used for that test?
Maya R: Config excerpt:
```
batcher.token_budget = 2048
batcher.prefill_window_ms = 40
batcher.max_hold_ms = 12
packer.hit_bias = true
packer.window_strategy = "size_then_time"
```
Arjun S: Two hypotheses: (1) hit_bias causes too much padding of hit-only microbatches, (2) token_budget target is tuned for non-hit workloads, so many small hit-only requests force more microbatching decisions.
Sanjay P: Agreed. Another angle: KV cache reduces per-request token count which reduces opportunity for continuous batching to amortize kernel setup. Packets are frequent but tiny.
Lisa T: Could try probabilistic-fill: don't wait deterministically to hit token_budget — instead use a time-weighted prob to flush based on recent hit fraction.
Kevin L: Like a PFW (probabilistic fill window) where flush chance p = clamp( alpha*hit_frac + beta*(age/ms), 0.02, 0.9 )?
Maya R: Yup. Also think about per-route token targets — routes with high cache-hit rates should have lower token_budget so they don't block.
Arjun S: I prototyped a tiny change: if hit_frac > 0.7, halve token_budget and reduce hold_ms by 50%. On a quick run latency p95 improved 9% and throughput recovered.
Maya R: Nice. Any regressions in throughput tail?
Arjun S: Slight increase in small-batch kernel launch overhead but overall better utilization.
Lisa T: We should add a kernel-selection signal for hit-heavy microbatches: prefer fast small-kernel (low setup) if detected, instead of forcing large-token kernels.
Kevin L: Sounds good. Steps: (1) add hit_frac metric to batcher metrics, (2) A/B test PFW with halved token_budget for hit-heavy routes, (3) add kernel signal to selector.
Maya R: I'll open the RFC and include perf traces + config + simple A/B plan.
deploy-bot: Deployed branch maya/pfw-proto to staging at 2130001280 :rocket:
Sanjay P: After staging run, let's collect `batch_fill_histogram`, `hit_frac_over_time`, `kernel_launch_count` and compare.
Maya R: Will do. Thanks all — I'll post the RFC link once it's up. :raised_hands:
